title: Upkeep: SC-040, SC-047
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: The broad rule 'no request header ever supplies scheme, host or client identity' was not widened to the bare X-Forwarded. The design only changes the narrow rule, which already applies to every non-test Go file, clientaddr.go included.

Holes pinned as quiet rows, not closed (lesson #939): a flag after an escaped \t inside an interpreted string (acc-br-q012); a flag at the start of a later line of a raw string (acc-br-q013); syscall.GetEnvironmentVariable (dt-env-q010); client-identity names that match no shape, such as X-Envoy-External-Address and CloudFront-Viewer-Address (fwn-q012, fwn-q017, cih-060..064); and underscore spellings (fwn-q018, cih-065..067).
internal/fitnessrules/** matches no architecture block's globs, so the package and its new files have no owner in the record. A person should say which block owns it, or whether none does.

Fitness op=check, which uses a real YAML parser, was not run: the builder has no such tool and this machine has no PyYAML. The edited because-texts are single-quoted with doubled apostrophes, the three new plain scalars have the same shape as the old ones, and TestFitnessYAMLPlainScalarsParse passes. The engine should still run op=check on the tree.

deviation: Rule 3 uses \.Environ\b instead of the prescribed \.Environ\(\). It is a superset: the same rows fire, and it also catches the method taken as a value (get := cmd.Environ). The rule's own because-text promises that it matches 'a call or a method value'. dt-env-f010 pins this. \.Environment stays quiet (dt-env-q009).

deviation: The finding's 'line 456' and 'line 457' are stale. The narrow rule's patterns are at lines 460 and 461 in this tree. I applied the prescribed regexes to those patterns (pattern 2 and pattern 3) and added the optional socket-?ip, so X-Azure-SocketIP now fires (fwn-f030, cih-030).

deviation: The class corpus for SC-040 is a new file with its own strict loader (client_identity_headers.json and client_identity_corpus_test.go) instead of more rule_spellings.json rows. A census of names expanded over quote styles, contexts and paths does not fit that file's one-text-per-row shape. The loader follows lesson #995. The four rows the finding names are also in rule_spellings.json. The SC-047 class corpus is rule_spellings.json itself.
